subject: Human Body
title: The Heart Muscle
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: The Heart Muscle.

hook.text: Cardiac muscle beats 3 billion times in an average lifetime. It never takes a break. Not once.

buildup.text: Cardiac cells are branched and interconnected. Electrical signals spread instantly, making the heart beat in unison.

discovery.text: The heart generates its own electrical rhythm. Remove it from the body and it keeps beating for a while.

twist.text: Cardiac muscle can't regenerate. A heart attack kills cells permanently. Scar tissue replaces them but can't contract.

climax.text: No other muscle combines the heart's endurance, coordination, and self-starting ability. It's in a class alone.

punchline.text: One muscle. Three billion beats. No vacations.

quiz.question: Why can the heart keep beating outside the body?
options: It stores enough blood to keep pumping
It generates its own electrical rhythm
It has a backup nerve supply
